{{short description|German mathematician}}
'''Heinrich Wilhelm Feodor Deahna''' (8 July 1815 – 8 January 1844) was a German mathematician.<ref name="adb">{{citation|last=Cantor|first=Moritz|contribution=Deahna, Heinrich Wilhelm Feodor|title=[[Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie]]|contribution-url=https://www.deutsche-biographie.de/ppn12290740X.html|volume=4|year=1876|at=S. 790|authorlink=Moritz Cantor}}.</ref>
He is known for providing proof of what is now known as [[Frobenius theorem (differential topology)|Frobenius theorem]] in [[differential topology]], which he published in [[Crelle's Journal]] in 1840.<ref>{{citation|title=The Mathematics of Frobenius in Context: A Journey Through 18th to 20th Century Mathematics|series=Sources and Studies in the History of Mathematics and Physical Sciences|first=Thomas|last=Hawkins|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|year=2013|isbn=9781461463337|page=188|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UzTBBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA188}}.</ref>

Deahna was born near [[Bayreuth]] on July 8, 1815, and was a student at the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1834. In 1843 he became an assistant mathematics teacher at the [[Fulda]] [[Gymnasium (Germany)|Gymnasium]], but he died soon afterwards in Fulda, on January 8, 1844.<ref name="adb"/>

== Selected works ==
* Deahna, F. "Über die Bedingungen der Integrabilitat ....", ''J. Reine Angew. Math.'' '''20''' (1840) 340-350.
